newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - April 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times front page - April 15.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following stories on its front page on Tuesday:
* U.S. Attorney General Janet Reno rejected Republican calls for an independent prosecutor to investigate President Bill Clinton's re-election campaign financings.

* James McDougal, the Whitewater business partner of Bill and Hillary Rodham Clinton, was sentenced to three years in prison by a federal judge for illegally obtaining millions of dollars in federally-backed loans in the 1980s.
* The Dow Jones industrials recovered some from its recent slide, finishing up about 60 points for the day.
* Many Russians, frustrated by the country's economic upheaval, are making Jews the scapegoats. Overt anti-semitism is mostly on the fringes of Russian society.
* British drugs company Zeneca has assumed management of 11 cancer centres it owns in U.S. hospitals.
* General Colin Powell, who keeps a hectic campaign schedule to encourage volunteers to help children, says he does not intend to run for U.S. President.
* Baseball player Jackie Robinson touched the lives of a generation of New Yorkers.
